title: Chaos Construction: Region Borders #1
author: udukos
rules:
I plan to publish two Chaos Construction puzzles using the following ruleset. This puzzle, along with the given example, is intended as an introduction to the rules. The main puzzle will follow in the coming days.
The region-building part can be a bit tricky, so I would recommend solving the example puzzle to get a feel for the logic.

Here are the rules:

Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of seven orthogonally connected cells. Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 7 once each.

Each circled digit indicates the total number of borders of its region encountered along straight lines extending outward from the cell’s four edges. Only edges along which a border runs are used as starting points. From each such edge, count all borders of the circled cell’s region along the straight line, stopping when a turn breaks the line. Note that the region borders on the edge of the grid count toward this total. There is no negative constraint (all possible circles are not given). There is a region border given between R1C2 AND R2C2. Looking at the solved 6x6 example should help make the rules much easier to understand.
